claim_1.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that many B cell subsets displayed low within-subject variability over more than two months compared to their inter-subject variability.

sources.quote: Among populations with high overall variability, many B cell subsets showed low within-subject variability (and therefore high temporal stability) over a period of more than two months (indicated in dark gray in Figure 2A).

Figure 2. Inter- and intra-subject variation at baseline (A) Variation in cell population frequencies at baseline. The length of the bar denotes observed sum-of-squares (R2). Blue and grey designate R2 attributed to inter- and intra-subject variation, respectively.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that subject-to-subject baseline differences contributed substantially to the observed variability of many genes and pathways compared to intra-subject variation.

sources.quote: Assessment of inter-vs. intra-subject variation demonstrated diverse patterns, with subject-to-subject baseline differences (blue bars) contributing substantially to the observed variability of many genes and pathways (Figures 2B and C).

Figure 2. Inter- and intra-subject variation at baseline (B) Variation in gene expression at baseline. Hierarchical-clustered heatmap of the 500 most variable genes and the relative proportion of inter- and intra-subject variation (see Methods). (C) Clustered heatmaps of genes from two variable immune relevant pathways showing distinct patterns of expression heterogeneity across subjects (see Figure S2C and Methods).

claim_3.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed increased influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As expected, we observed strong, but highly variable, increases in influenza vaccine-specific IgG+ antibody secreting cells on day 7 (Figure 3A).
Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (A) Increased antigen-specific antibody secreting cells on day 7 following vaccination measured by ELISpot.

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at days 1, 7, and 70 post-vaccination, using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that gene-expression changes on day 1 and day 7 were largely non-overlapping compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As previously reported (Bucasas et al., 2011; Nakaya et al., 2011; Obermoser et al., 2013), we also found coherent changes in gene expression, with largely non-overlapping signatures on days 1 and 7 (Figures 3B and 3C).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (B) Heatmap of genes from days -7, 1, 7 and 70 that changed significantly compared to day 0 (FDR<0.05 and absolute log-fold-change > 0.2; fold-change from day 0 is indicated by color). Genes with similar patterns of change were grouped by clustering analysis (indicated by the color bars on the left.) (C) Coherently changed genes in the clusters from B. Right: Representative immunological pathways enriched in coherently changing genes on days 1 and 7 (see Methods).

claim_5.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 1 post-vaccination (day 1), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that day 1 responses included innate immune-cell activation pathways including Interferon-related genes compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Overall, day 1 responses included pathways reflecting innate immune-cell activation, including Interferon-related genes, as observed by others (Bucasas et al., 2011; Nakaya et al., 2011; Obermoser et al., 2013) (Figure 3C and Table S3).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (C) Coherently changed genes in the clusters from B. Right: Representative immunological pathways enriched in coherently changing genes on days 1 and 7 (see Methods).

claim_6.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that adaptive pathways including Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress and N-glycan biosynthesis were more predominant compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: By day 7, adaptive pathways were more predominant, including those strongly associated with plasmablasts, such as “Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) stress” and “N-glycan biosynthesis” (see below) (Gass et al., 2004; Iwakoshi et al., 2003).

claim_7.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at days 1 and 7 post-vaccination showed that changes in cell-subset frequencies on day 1 and day 7 were largely non-overlapping compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: As with the transcriptome, changes in subset frequencies on days 1 and 7 were largely non-overlapping (Figure 3D).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_8.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 1 post-vaccination (day 1) showed that CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes (ID65 and ID67), IFNα+ plasmacytoid DCs (ID78), activated CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, and both naïve and memory B cells changed coherently compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Again, day 1 changes reflected activation of innate immune cells, including CD40+ and CD86+ monocytes (ID65 and ID67) and IFNa+ plasmacytoid DCs (ID78), populations that have been linked to vaccination efficacy and responses to influenza (Fonteneau et al., 2003; van Duin et al., 2007). However, we also observed changes in adaptive cell populations, particularly those reflecting activation of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, as well as both naïve and memory B cells (Kaminski et al., 2012).

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_9.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed that plasmablasts (ID87), a related CD20+CD27+CD38+ B-cell subset (ID96), and activated T-cell populations changed coherently compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Day 7 responses primarily reflected changes in adaptive cell populations, including plasmablasts (ID87) as expected, but also a related CD20+ B subset that expressed CD27 and CD38 (ID96, Figure S3), as well as activated T cell populations.

Figure 3. Post-vaccination changes in serologic, cellular and transcriptomic parameters (D) Coherently-changed cell populations on days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (FDR<0.05 and >10% change from day 0). Blue and brown boxes denote populations considered “innate” and “adaptive”, respectively.

claim_10.claim: Microneutralization assay analysis of serum from 63 healthy volunteers at day 70 post-vaccination (day 70) showed that day 70/day 0 fold-change in titer was positively associated with the day 7 fold-change in titer.

sources.quote: Since the day 70-day 0 fold-change in titer correlated with both the day 7 fold-change in titer and effector B cell responses, and thus reflected both short- and long-term responses (Figures S4B and S4C), we used day 70 titer responses as the endpoint for subsequent analyses.

claim_11.claim: Microneutralization assay analysis of serum from 63 healthy volunteers at day 70 post-vaccination (day 70) showed that day 70/day 0 fold-change in titer was positively associated with ELISpot day 7 effector B-cell responses.

sources.quote: Since the day 70-day 0 fold-change in titer correlated with both the day 7 fold-change in titer and effector B cell responses, and thus reflected both short- and long-term responses (Figures S4B and S4C), we used day 70 titer responses as the endpoint for subsequent analyses.

claim_12.claim: Microneutralization assay analysis of serum from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 and day 70 post-vaccination showed that subjects with higher initial titers had lower day 70/day 0 fold-changes in titer compared to subjects with lower initial titers.

sources.quote: Interestingly, subjects with higher initial titers tended to have lower fold-changes.

Figure 4. Post-vaccination responses depend on baseline serology and memory B-cell status (A) Relationship between initial and fold-change (day 70/day 0) in titer for A/Uruguay after vaccination (see Figure S4 for other viruses). Histogram at left shows distribution of the titer responses.

claim_13.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 59 healthy volunteers in baseline serology/memory B-cell group 1 (n=33) and group 2 (n=26) at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) in the more naïve group 1 compared to group 2.

sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).

Figure 4. Post-vaccination responses depend on baseline serology and memory B-cell status (B) Heatmap showing two distinct groups of subjects identified based on robust clustering analysis of day 0 serologic and memory B-cell variables (see Methods) (C) Post-vaccination changes in plasmablast frequencies on day 7 for the low (1) and high (2) initial titer groups from B.

claim_14.claim: ELISpot analysis of PBMCs from 59 healthy volunteers in baseline serology/memory B-cell group 1 (n=33) and group 2 (n=26) at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed greater increases in seasonal vaccine-specific IgG responses in the more naïve group 1 compared to group 2.

sources.quote: However, the more naïve group exhibited significantly greater increases in plasmablasts (ID87) and seasonal vaccine-specific ELISpot responses on day 7 (Figure 4C).

Figure 4. Post-vaccination responses depend on baseline serology and memory B-cell status (B) Heatmap showing two distinct groups of subjects identified based on robust clustering analysis of day 0 serologic and memory B-cell variables (see Methods) (C) Post-vaccination changes in plasmablast frequencies on day 7 for the low (1) and high (2) initial titer groups from B.

claim_15.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7), after removing age, gender, and race effects by linear regression, showed that plasmablasts (ID87) and the overlapping CD20+IgD-CD27+CD38+ B-cell subpopulation (ID96) were the dominant cellular contributors to prediction of day 70 antibody-response endpoints compared to other day 7 cell populations.

sources.quote: Accordingly, plasmablasts (ID87) and the overlapping CD20+ subpopulation (ID96) were the dominant cellular contributors (Figure 5E) (Withers et al., 2007).

Figure 5. Predictive modeling of antibody response and identification of correlates (E) Day 7 predictive cell populations (see Results and Methods). The percentage of times (from 5000 random trials) a cell population is included in the model is shown. Median normalized weights of each population are shown on the right. The sign of the weight indicates the direction of correlation between the cell population and the titer endpoint.

claim_16.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 1 post-vaccination (day 1), after removing age, gender, and race effects by linear regression and using pathway enrichment analysis, showed that Interferon Signaling was positively associated with the microneutralization assay maximum fold-change (MFC) day 70 antibody-response endpoint.

sources.quote: While models built using either gene expression or cell populations from day 1 were not predictive, “Interferon Signaling” correlated robustly with MFC (Figure 5C).

Figure 5. Predictive modeling of antibody response and identification of correlates (C) Robust transcriptomic correlates from days 1 and 7 post-vaccination (shown as pathway enrichments) (see Methods). Percentage of times a pathway is enriched (p<0.05) is shown. Pathways significant for more than 80% of the trials for at least one time-point are shown.

claim_17.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7), after removing age, gender, and race effects by linear regression, showed that day 7 gene-expression data predicted both adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) and maximum fold-change (MFC) day 70 antibody-response endpoints compared to chance.

sources.quote: In contrast, highly predictive models could be built using day 7 data for both adjMFC and MFC (Figures 5D).

Figure 5. Predictive modeling of antibody response and identification of correlates (D) Prediction performance for MFC and adjMFC shown for models built using different number of top cell-populations (D) and genes (F) from day 7 (see Methods).

claim_18.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7), after removing age, gender, and race effects by linear regression, showed that maximum fold-change (MFC) could be predicted using as few as 2 or 5 genes compared to chance.

sources.quote: Consistent with previous findings (Nakaya et al., 2011), MFC could be predicted using as few as 2 or 5 genes, although more were required for adjMFC (Figure 5F).

Figure 5. Predictive modeling of antibody response and identification of correlates (D) Prediction performance for MFC and adjMFC shown for models built using different number of top cell-populations (D) and genes (F) from day 7 (see Methods).

claim_19.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), after removing age, gender, and ancestry effects by linear regression, showed that genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling were positively associated with the microneutralization assay maximum fold-change (MFC) day 70 antibody-response endpoint, but less strongly with adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC).

sources.quote: Notably, genes associated with pattern recognition and Interferon signaling robustly correlated to MFC, but less so to adjMFC.
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (A) Robust correlates between day 0 gene expression and response titers (see Figure 5C).

claim_20.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), after removing age, gender, and ancestry effects by linear regression, showed that day 0 cell-population frequencies alone predicted maximum fold-change (MFC) and adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) day 70 antibody-response endpoints compared to chance.

sources.quote: Notably, predictive models could be built by using cell populations alone (Figure 6B)—integrating pathway/transcript with cell population data performed substantially worse (best median AUC was 0.6 vs. 0.78 using cell populations alone). Thus, day 0 cell frequencies alone provided the essential information for prediction.
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (B) Prediction performance using day 0 populations (as in Figure 5D).

claim_21.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), after removing age, gender, and ancestry effects by linear regression, showed that integrating pathway/transcript data with cell-population data predicted day 70 antibody-response endpoints less accurately than using cell populations alone.

assay.link_note: The comparison is about integrated models combining day 0 cell-population frequencies with pathway/transcript-derived features versus cell populations alone; the finding is not generated by flow cytometry alone but by downstream integrative modeling across assays.

sources.quote: Notably, predictive models could be built by using cell populations alone (Figure 6B)—integrating pathway/transcript with cell population data performed substantially worse (best median AUC was 0.6 vs. 0.78 using cell populations alone).
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (B) Prediction performance using day 0 populations (as in Figure 5D).

claim_22.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), after removing age, gender, and ancestry effects by linear regression, showed that twelve cell populations including memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNα+ myeloid dendritic cells, and several activated T-cell populations predicted adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) day 70 antibody responses compared to non-predictive cell populations.

sources.quote: Twelve cell populations were identified for adjMFC, including memory, naïve and transitional B cells, CD4 effector memory T cells, IFNα+ myeloid dendritic cells (mDC), and several activated T cell populations (Figure 6C; see Methods).
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (C) Day 0 predictive cell populations analyzed as in Figure 5E.

claim_23.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), after removing age, gender, and ancestry effects by linear regression, showed that only some day 0 predictive populations, primarily T-cell subsets, predicted maximum fold-change (MFC) day 70 antibody responses compared to adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) predictors.

sources.quote: Only some of these populations, primarily the T cell subsets, contributed to the prediction of MFC (Figure 6C). Thus, by accounting for baseline serology using adjMFC, we uncovered additional baseline predictors.
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (C) Day 0 predictive cell populations analyzed as in Figure 5E.

claim_24.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that all predictive B-cell populations except ID105, together with some predictive CD4+ T-cell populations including effector memory cells, were remarkably stable within individuals over more than two months compared to their inter-subject variation.

sources.quote: Except for ID105 (CD86+IgD+ memory B cells), all of the B cell and some of the CD4+ T cell (including effector memory) predictive populations were remarkably stable within individuals over a period of more than two months (Figure 6D).

Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (D) Scatter plot of intra-subject stability (y) vs. inter-subject variance (x) (see Methods). Predictive populations from (C) are highlighted in blue (more stable populations) and yellow (less stable).

claim_25.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that B-cell subsets including ID103 and ID91 had some of the highest inter-subject variation among measured cell populations compared to other cell populations.

sources.quote: Among these were B cell subsets that also exhibited some of the highest inter-subject variation among all of the cell populations we measured (e.g., ID103 and 91; Figure 2A), suggesting these may be robust baseline markers for delineating inter-subject differences.

Figure 2. Inter- and intra-subject variation at baseline (A) Variation in cell population frequencies at baseline. The length of the bar denotes observed sum-of-squares (R2). Blue and grey designate R2 attributed to inter- and intra-subject variation, respectively.

claim_26.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that the stable CD38+ B-cell populations ID91, ID96, ID103, and ID108 predicted adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) but not maximum fold-change (MFC) day 70 antibody responses.

sources.quote: These stable B-cell populations (ID91, 96, 103, 108) were all CD38+ and contributed to the prediction of adjMFC but not MFC.

claim_27.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, 7, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that predictive cell populations remained able to separate high and low adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) responders compared to each other over time.

sources.quote: Examining the predictive cell populations' temporal profile further confirmed their stability and ability to separate the high and low responders (Figures 6E, 6F and S5).

Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (E-F) Temporal profiles of two stable predictive cell populations for high (orange) and low (green) responders (based on adjMFC). Missing data points correspond to samples with low viability.

claim_28.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at days 0, 7, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that ID96 increased coherently across subjects at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) and returned to lower levels by day 70 compared to day 7.

sources.quote: This was true even for ID96, which increased coherently across subjects at day 7 post-vaccination and returned to lower levels by day 70.

claim_29.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), using only the 56 most stable populations, showed that adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) day 70 antibody responses could be robustly predicted compared to chance.

sources.quote: Even using a smaller k of 10 (versus 30 previously), adjMFC could be robustly predicted (median AUC=0.78; Figure 6G).
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (G) Predictive performance for day 0 using only the temporally stable populations (those above the 80% mark in Figure 6D).

claim_30.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), using only the 56 most stable populations, showed that maximum fold-change (MFC) day 70 antibody-response prediction decreased compared to prediction using all day 0 cell populations.

sources.quote: In contrast, use of the stable cell populations decreased the predictive performance for MFC, which remained flat for all values of k.
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (G) Predictive performance for day 0 using only the temporally stable populations (those above the 80% mark in Figure 6D).

claim_31.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0), omitting the stable populations above the 80% stability mark, showed that maximum fold-change (MFC) day 70 antibody responses remained highly predictable whereas adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) prediction dropped substantially compared to models including the stable populations.

sources.quote: However, if the stable populations above the 80% mark in Figure 6D were omitted instead, performance remained high for MFC (median AUC=0.83 for k=10), but dropped substantially for adjMFC (median AUC=0.56 for k=10).
Figure 6. Day 0 predictors and correlates (G) Predictive performance for day 0 using only the temporally stable populations (those above the 80% mark in Figure 6D).

claim_32.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at baseline days -7, 0, and 70 relative to vaccination (day 0), using day 0 cell-population data as the training set, showed that adjusted maximum fold-change (adjMFC) could be accurately predicted from independent baseline measurements at day -7 and day 70 compared to chance.

sources.quote: Highly accurate prediction could still be made for all k's, e.g., AUC=0.91 and AUC=0.86 for days -7 and 70 using k=10, respectively. Thus, the predictive signals were remarkably stable over time.

claim_33.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed that plasmablasts (ID87) and the predictive CD20+IgD-CD27+CD38+ B-cell population (ID96) were positively associated with antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes including Ig chains, XBP1, and IRF4, and with ER stress and N-glycan biosynthesis pathways.

sources.quote: As expected, the two predictive and coherently changing cell populations from day 7 (ID87 and ID96) were linked to known antigen secreting cell/B cell/plasmablast-specific genes, including Ig chains, XBP1 and IRF4, as well as plasmablast-associated pathways such as ER stress (Figures 7B and D).

These populations were also associated with N-glycan biosynthesis, consistent with the highly glycosylated state of immunoglobulins and the requirement for proper glycosylation for plasma cell development (Tulp et al., 1986).

Figure 7. Gene expression and pathway enrichment signatures of predictive cell populations Genes significantly correlated with predictive populations from (A) day 0 and (B) day 7. In (B), coherently changing genes from Figure 3 are highlighted by color denoting the clusters from Figure 3B. Analyses were performed separately for positively and negatively correlated genes (in red and blue scales respectively). Only genes significantly correlated with at least one population are shown (FDR<0.01). Pathway enrichment analyses of gene correlates of (C) day 0 and (D) day 7 predictive cell populations (from Figure 6C).

claim_34.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed that many plasmablast-correlated genes were also genes that changed on day 7 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: Many plasmablast-correlated genes were also ones that changed on day 7 (Figures 3B, C and 7B (marked in purple and orange)) and included genes found to be predictive of or correlated with response titers in previous studies (marked in blue; e.g., TNFRSF17).

claim_35.claim: Flow cytometric analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 7 post-vaccination (day 7) showed that plasmablast frequencies were positively associated with microarray day 7 genes from ER stress, cell cycle, and N-glycan biosynthesis pathways.

assay.link_note: This is a cross-assay association claim linking plasmablast frequencies to day 7 microarray-derived gene/pathway signatures; it is not generated by flow cytometry alone.

sources.quote: Notably, robustly correlated (Figure 5C) and predictive genes (Table S4) were enriched for “ER stress”, “N-glycan biosynthesis” and cell cycle pathways, whose gene members correlated strongly with plasmablast frequencies (see below).

claim_36.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 before vaccination (day 0) showed that several mitochondria-related pathways were positively associated with the frequencies of ID108 (CD38+ naïve B cells) and ID91 (CD38hi transitional B cells).

sources.quote: Several mitochondria-related pathways were positively associated with ID108 (CD38+ naïve B cells) and ID91 (CD38hi transitional B cells), perhaps reflecting changes in bioenergetic states associated with B cell development and activation.

sources.quote: Of note, several innate pathways (PRR signaling, TREM1 signaling, and interferon-related genes) were positively linked to IL22+ and IL2+ CD4+ T cells (ID25 and ID26), and negatively linked to ID36 and ID50.

Pathway enrichment analyses of gene correlates of (C) day 0 and (D) day 7 predictive cell populations (from Figure 6C).

claim_38.claim: Microarray analysis of PBMCs from 63 healthy volunteers at day 0 and day 7 relative to vaccination (day 0) showed that the predictive B-cell population ID96 had largely distinct transcriptomic signatures on day 0 compared to day 7.

sources.quote: Interestingly, ID96, a day 0 predictive B-cell population that also coherently increased on day 7 (Figures 3D and 6F), showed largely distinct signatures on days 0 and 7 (Figures 7A-D), suggesting differences in the cell population defined by those markers, or distinct functional interactions with other cell populations post-vaccination.
